set.body: These modules call cliWrappers.ts's callLLM directly, which uses Bun.spawn -- only callable from a real Bun process, never from browser-executed React code (Bun is undefined in the browser; confirmed via typeof Bun === 'undefined' in a live browser test). DiagramGenExtension.tsx hit this exact bug during epic C story 1 and was fixed by routing through src/lib/llmClient.ts (Tauri run_llm_cli command, or the dev server's POST /api/llm) instead of calling cliWrappers.callLLM directly. set.body: DOMPurify's svg-only sanitize profile in src/lib/sanitize.ts hard-excludes the foreignObject tag (a known SVG XSS vector), which is how Mermaid renders flowchart/state-diagram node labels (HTML span/p inside foreignObject, not plain SVG <text>). Result: node shapes render but all label text is silently stripped. Fixed by adding the html DOMPurify profile, ADD_TAGS:['foreignobject'], and HTML_INTEGRATION_POINTS:{foreignobject:true} (DOMPurify enforces HTML-in-SVG namespace rules independently of the tag allowlist). Verified live: flowchart labels (Start/Is it working?/Yes/No/Great!/Debug) now render correctly.
set.title: sanitizeSvg strips Mermaid's HTML-based node labels (foreignObject), leaving diagrams with empty shapes and no text

set.body: Observed while live-verifying the sanitizeSvg fix: when an AI-generated diagram has invalid Mermaid syntax, DiagramGenExtension.tsx correctly catches the error and shows its own inline message, but mermaid.render() itself also has a side effect of appending a bomb-icon error overlay to document.body -- outside any of our React-managed containers, appearing as a stray fixed-position toast unrelated to the failing block's on-screen position. Cosmetic, not a data-loss or security issue; low priority. Would need to intercept/suppress mermaid's own DOM-injecting error path (e.g. via its internal error renderer config) or remove the stray node after each render attempt.
set.title: Mermaid's internal parse-error UI ('bomb' error graphic) injects into document.body instead of staying inside the failing block's container

set.body: Decision (user-confirmed): use the locally-installed `imagen` CLI (wraps Google's Gemini Imagen API, already configured with a working API key on this machine). Images are stored as base64 data URIs directly on the node's src attribute (ponytail: mirrors how DiagramGenExtension stores rendered content inline; avoids needing workspace-relative file paths / Tauri asset-protocol plumbing for v1 -- upgrade path is real file storage if doc-size bloat becomes a problem). Verified end-to-end live in-browser with a real (non-mocked) imagen call producing a real 1408px PNG.

set.body: Found by the first console baseline measurement in Phase 0. The welcome document serializes an unset diagram as 'content: null'. Three extensions each carried their own copy of the key:value parser, and all three turned that into the 4-character string "null" -- truthy, so DiagramGenExtension's render guard let it through and mermaid threw UnknownDiagramError on every page load. Fixed by extracting one shared parser (blockAttrs.ts) treating serialized null/undefined as unset, and pointing Dataset/ImageGen/DiagramGen at it. ImageGen had the same latent defect via 'src: null'.

set.body: Found while proving the E2E network gate actually bites. server.ts fell through to the SPA shell for ANY unmatched path, so fetch() for a missing note returned HTTP 200 carrying a page of HTML. WebStorage.readFile checks res.ok, so it treated that as a successful read and handed the editor HTML source as the note's markdown -- worse than the 'error loading file' behaviour B2 was thought to have. It also made missing files structurally invisible to the network gate. Fixed: unknown /api/* returns 404 JSON, a missing path whose last segment has a file extension returns 404, and only extensionless routes fall through to the SPA shell. /favicon.ico now answers 204 so the browser's unprompted request is not gate noise.

set.body: Bun.serve defaults to hostname 0.0.0.0 when none is given, so the dev server listened on every interface. It already exposed /api/llm and /api/image, which spawn local subprocesses, and Phase 1 added /api/fs/write on top -- so anything on the same network could write files inside the workspace and run CLI tools, with no authentication. The workspace jail constrains where a write lands; it says nothing about who may ask. Now binds 127.0.0.1, overridable via MOTION_HOST. Also removed the Google Fonts entries still sitting in the Tauri CSP after the font links were dropped -- permissions granted for something the app no longer does. Surfaced by the design-doc generation pass reading the code end to end.

set.body: Opening a saved document with custom block node views logged 'flushSync was called from inside a lifecycle method' at console.error level, three times per load. Fixed per Tiptap's own performance guide by deferring the state update with queueMicrotask. Only surfaced because one E2E spec saved a document with blocks into a file another spec then opened -- the console gate caught it immediately.

set.body: Three independent usability gaps found while dogfooding the motion CLI. First, 'motion note.md' exits with an error because the CLI only accepts directories, so the natural way to open a note fails. Second, nothing in the app tracks unsaved edits, so clicking another note in the sidebar silently throws away in-flight work. Third, there is no way to change text size, and the setting should be remembered between sessions. Save itself already works and is out of scope.

set.body: Running the desktop launcher twice starts a second app window whose bundled dev server cannot bind its port, because the first instance already holds it. The second window then quietly connects to the first instance's server and shows the wrong workspace, with no error anywhere the user can see. Browser mode already searches for a free port when the configured one is busy; desktop mode does not. Either reuse the running server deliberately when it already serves the requested folder, or find a free port and pass it through, and fail loudly rather than silently attaching to someone else's workspace.
set.title: Second desktop instance silently shows the wrong workspace
